Let's start with the good: It's a really fun game with an interesting story and really good gameplay. The puzzles were interesting and pretty creative. The voice acting was well done and the UI felt nice to use. 
Also, unlike most other games like this, this game does at least try to be accurate with it's technology. Some creative liberties are taken, but as a technically minded person I wasn't screaming "That's not how that works!" all the time.

Now for my main issue: This game is way too short for the price. The game took me 4 hours and that was without trying to go fast. If I tried I feel like this game could be 100% in less that 3 hours (maybe even <2h).
It's not a full $60 game, but even for $15 this is just too short. And the story ends right as it starts getting interesting. Right after some actual intrigue is revealed the credits roll.
Another issue is that it's very linear. It doesn't matter what you do, there is only a single ending. The different options only affect which 10 second response you'll get and nothing after that.

I don't think it's worth getting this game for the full price, but if it's for sale for <$10 it's an alright deal.

A Thriller That Rekindled My Creative Spark

🖥️ 🔍 ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆
🕹️ Great on Steam Deck

One of the reasons I became a software developer was the dream of eventually making games. Over the years, there have only been a handful of titles that truly reignited that spark and made game development feel possible again. The Operator unexpectedly became one of those games.

From its presentation to its atmosphere, the game pulled me in quickly, but it was the storytelling, especially toward the final stretch, that really hit. The ending was a genuine chef’s kiss. Not because it wrapped everything neatly, but because it didn’t. When it was over, I felt that familiar disappointment that only comes from wanting more. More answers about HAL. More about The Ghost. More about the Organization and where this world could go next.

I understand why some players felt like they were simply going through the motions to push the story forward. For me, curiosity carried the experience. I wanted to poke at every decision, even knowing the branching paths were not especially deep or wide. The choices still felt meaningful enough to keep me engaged and questioning the outcome.

If you’re looking for a short, focused thriller with an intriguing premise, believable characters, and a strong audiovisual presentation, The Operator is absolutely worth your time. Especially on sale. It’s the kind of game that lingers in your head after the credits roll, and quietly nudges your creative mind into motion.

[h3]TL;DR[/h3]
Very nice game but very short with no replayability so highly recommended, but I'd suggest on discounted price.


[h3]Details[/h3]
Very well written, very well executed game with little to no bugs (bumped into an issue for which I had to ALT+F4 and start over a scene, but nothing else). Great effects, great story, good music.

[h3]A bit off, but[/h3]
I hope the code was written with generalization in mind, so it's less effort to release a 2nd game, which I hope will happen some time, maybe even soon. I could imagine a game in which (maybe even as DLCs) a number of cases have to be investigated / solved in the very same way & format this story worked out.


[h3]Negatives[/h3]
More feedback than 'downvote material' as again, the game is great, but there's always room for improvement, right?

A short game that puts you in the chair of a government operator working remotely to aid agents and uncover a mystery.

This game is dripping with immersion, from sound to mechanics. The operator PC is an excellent tool in both storytelling and in making you feel like you're operating the computer yourself. Although not too in-depth, what it does do with the concept it succeeds - so much so that I honestly wish this was a much longer detective-style game that allowed you to do more missions, but what it does have is enough for the story.
When it comes to the story, it's pretty good. It's a nice blend of suspense and mystery that feels like an interactive spy thriller with a more grounded feel. The voice-acting is excellent with a believable quality to it, and the pacing/presentation is excellently done. There's not much in replayability, but I think the story does a great enough job nonetheless.

When it comes to achievements/completion, it's good. Some of the achievements are missable and require very specific actions - though nothing so crazy that you feel the need to replay it just to get it.

Overall I really do recommend this game. If you want a short and effective story with some good investigative elements, I think this is worth getting.

The Operator is a 5/10 for me. I just didn’t like it, and the ending honestly pissed me off. It felt dumb. I went into this game thinking I’d be connecting the dots, using my brain, cracking a case, or at least acting like the man in the chair. I expected some detective-style depth, and yeah, I knew there’d be a story, but not this kind of story.

Gameplay & Expectations
I watched the trailer, played the demo, and at first I was excited. The gameplay itself was fun for what it was, and I thought it would build into something bigger. Instead, it just… ended. The ending was surprising, sure, but it wasn’t good. It left me feeling like all that build-up led nowhere.

Replay Value
There’s barely any replay value. No unlimited mode, no side content, nothing to keep you going after finishing the story. And if I remember correctly, there’s not much you can do to actually change the ending, so I had zero motivation to replay it.

Final Thoughts
It’s a fun little game on sale, but I’d recommend watching a video and playing the demo before you consider buying it. Once I beat it, I felt completely done with
